title: Proper direct-image restriction comparison and its scalar counit square
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings and $h:Z\to Y$ a morphism of schemes. Use ordinary uncompleted unbounded derived categories $D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ of modules over the constant ring sheaf $R_W$, for $W=Z,Y$ and $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $T_W=-\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$ and let $r_W$ be exact scalar restriction, with the representative-normalized adjunction $T_W\dashv r_W$ and counit $\epsilon_W$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Write $P_R=h_R^*$, $R_R=Rh_{*,R}$ and $e^R:P_RR_R\to1$ for the canonical geometric adjunction counit [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $\chi:P_BT_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}T_ZP_A$ be the canonical balanced tensor/pullback comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], computed on K-flat representatives. Let $d:r_YR_B\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Ar_Z$ be the normalized ring-sheaf comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] and put $D=d^{-1}$. Define $\gamma_N:T_YR_AN\to R_BT_ZN$ by its geometric transpose
$$e^B_{T_ZN}\circ P_B(\gamma_N)=T_Z(e^A_N)\circ\chi_{R_AN}.$$
Then $\gamma$ is natural in every $N\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. The composite adjunctions $P_BT_Y\dashv r_YR_B$ and $T_ZP_A\dashv R_Ar_Z$, with canonical left comparison $\chi$ and right comparison $D^{-1}$, satisfy for every $H\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$
$$e^B_H\circ P_B(\epsilon_Y(R_BH))\circ\chi^{-1}_{r_YR_BH}=\epsilon_Z(H)\circ T_Z(e^A_{r_ZH})\circ T_ZP_A(D_H^{-1}).$$
Their specified comparisons therefore satisfy the scalar counit square
$$\epsilon_Y(R_BH)\circ T_Y(D_H)=R_B(\epsilon_Z(H))\circ\gamma_{r_ZH}.$$
Moreover $D$ is exactly the direct-image restriction comparison of [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]: for a K-injective $B_Z$-complex $I$ and a K-injective resolution $r_ZI\to I'$ over $A_Z$, $D_I$ is the inverse of the class of $r_Yh_*I=h_*r_ZI\to h_*I'$, under the canonical resolution identifications. This identification uses the same direct-image composition normalization $\kappa$ as [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. All equations hold without properness of $h$, flatness of $B/A$, or boundedness or finite Tor amplitude of $H$ or $r_ZH$.

proof.text:
Let $\eta^B:1\to R_BP_B$ be the unit of the specified geometric adjunction. Its Hom bijection gives the unique arrow with the required transpose, explicitly
$$\gamma_N=R_B\bigl(T_Z(e^A_N)\circ\chi_{R_AN}\bigr)\circ\eta^B_{T_YR_AN}.$$
For $v:N\to N'$, naturality of $e^A$ and $\chi$ gives
$$T_Z(v)\circ T_Z(e^A_N)\circ\chi_{R_AN}=T_Z(e^A_{N'})\circ\chi_{R_AN'}\circ P_BT_YR_A(v).$$
Naturality of the geometric Hom bijection therefore gives $R_BT_Z(v)\circ\gamma_N=\gamma_{N'}\circ T_YR_A(v)$. This proves existence, uniqueness and naturality without assuming that $\gamma$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; naturality of the Hom bijection.

proof.text:
Use the isomorphism $b:r_ZP_B\xrightarrow{\sim}P_Ar_Y$ supplied by the ring-sheaf change adjunction, with the canonical constant-coefficient identifications $c_A,c_B$ used by $P_A,P_B$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Writing $\varphi:A\to B$ and $\varphi_W:A_W\to B_W$ for the induced map, the ring-square hypothesis of that node, $\varphi_Zc_A=c_Bh^{-1}\varphi_Y$, holds: the adjoints of both sides send each constant section $a$ to $\eta_Z(\varphi(a))$, and a locally constant section is glued from constant sections on its open fibres. Apply that node's adjunct equation to $M=R_BH$, $N=H$ and $t=e^B_H$. The geometric adjunct of $t$ is $1_{R_BH}$ by the triangle identity. Its assertion thus reads
$$r_Z(e^B_H)\circ b_{R_BH}^{-1}=e^A_{r_ZH}\circ P_A(d_H).$$
This uses the normalized $d$ of the statement, rather than choosing a new right-adjoint isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; specified restriction/pullback adjunct compatibility.

proof.text:
For $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ the scalar counits satisfy
$$P_B(\epsilon_Y(K))\circ\chi^{-1}_{r_YK}=\epsilon_Z(P_BK)\circ T_Z(b_K^{-1}).\tag{*}$$
Here is the representative check, including the derived identifications. Represent $K$ by a $B_Y$-complex $C$ and choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $g:P\to r_YC$. Since $P_A$ is exact, $P_Ag$ is a quasi-isomorphism onto $P_Ar_YC$; its source $P_AP$ is K-flat with flat terms by pullback preservation. Consequently $b_C^{-1}P_Ag:P_AP\to r_ZP_BC$ is an admissible resolution for the scalar counit on $Z$. The scalar-adjunction normalization computes that counit by $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,b_C^{-1}P_Ag(x)$. On the other side, the counit on $Y$ is $p\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(p)$, and the specified balanced $\chi^{-1}$ carries $x\otimes b$ to the inverse image of $p\otimes b$ when $x=h^{-1}p$. Thus both maps in (*) are the same $B_Z$-linear extension of $b_C^{-1}P_Ag$ from $P_AP$. This equality is a sheaf-tensor equality by its universal property, not an assertion that all sections are single tensors. Applying localization and cancelling the common invertible resolution comparisons proves (*) for $K$.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat; Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; Tag 03EL, sites-modules lemma-tensor-product-pullback. Explicit balanced-tensor calculation.

proof.text:
The counits of the two composite adjunctions are $e^B_H\circ P_B(\epsilon_Y(R_BH))$ and $\epsilon_Z(H)\circ T_Z(e^A_{r_ZH})$, respectively. Substitute (*) with $K=R_BH$ into the first, after precomposing with $\chi^{-1}$. Naturality of $\epsilon_Z$ at $e^B_H$ and then the equation of step 2 give
$$\begin{aligned}
e^B_H\circ P_B(\epsilon_Y(R_BH))\circ\chi^{-1}_{r_YR_BH}
&=\epsilon_Z(H)\circ T_Z\bigl(r_Z(e^B_H)\circ b_{R_BH}^{-1}\bigr)\\
&=\epsilon_Z(H)\circ T_Z(e^A_{r_ZH})\circ T_ZP_A(d_H).
\end{aligned}$$
Since $d=D^{-1}$, this is exactly the stated equation for the specified composite adjunctions.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; elementary substitution into the composite-adjunction counit formula.

proof.text:
For the scalar square, apply the injective geometric transposition map $u\mapsto e^B_H\circ P_B(u)$ to the two arrows from $T_YR_Ar_ZH$ to $R_BH$. The transpose of $\epsilon_Y(R_BH)\circ T_Y(D_H)$, using step 4 and naturality of $\chi^{-1}$ at $D_H$, is
$$\epsilon_Z(H)\circ T_Z(e^A_{r_ZH})\circ\chi_{R_Ar_ZH};$$
indeed the adjacent factors $T_ZP_A(d_H)$ and $T_ZP_A(D_H)$ cancel. The transpose of $R_B(\epsilon_Z(H))\circ\gamma_{r_ZH}$ is the same expression, by naturality of $e^B$ and the defining transpose equation of $\gamma$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection proves the scalar counit square, with both sides natural in $H$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; equality of geometric transposes and cancellation of d composed with D.

proof.text:
Finally identify the comparison on resolutions. Let $a_W:(W,B_W)\to(W,A_W)$ be the identity-topos coefficient morphisms and let $k=h_Aa_Z=a_Yh_B$. Exact scalar restriction is the direct image of $a_W$. By the stated meaning of the ring-sheaf comparison,
$$d=\kappa_{h_A,a_Z}\circ\kappa_{a_Y,h_B}^{-1}:r_YR_B\longrightarrow R_Ar_Z.$$
For a K-injective $B_Z$-complex $I$ and a K-injective resolution $j:r_ZI\to I'$ over $A_Z$, the resolution clause of $\kappa_{h_A,a_Z}$ represents its component by $h_*j:r_Yh_*I=h_*r_ZI\to h_*I'$, and asserts that this is a quasi-isomorphism. The other factor, $\kappa_{a_Y,h_B}$, identifies $Rk(I)$ with $r_YR_B(I)$; since $r_Y$ is exact, its resolution comparison cancels under the canonical termwise restriction identifications. Thus $d_I$ is exactly the displayed class of $h_*j$, and $D_I$ is its inverse. This is precisely the comparison characterized in the direct-image restriction node. Naturality of $\kappa$ extends the identification through resolution isomorphisms to every derived object. No step assumes that $r_ZI$ itself is K-injective, nor uses properness, flatness, boundedness or finite Tor amplitude.
